name: Question 20
worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the sum and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4{x}^{3}{y}^{2}-{e}^{2y}{z}^{4}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4{x}^{3}{y}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{2y}{z}^{4}) \\  & =4{x}^{3}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})-{z}^{4}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{2y})\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the chain rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})-{z}^{4}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{2y}) & =4{x}^{3}\cdot 2y-{z}^{4}\cdot {e}^{2y}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(2y) \\  & =4{x}^{3}\cdot 2y-{z}^{4}\cdot {e}^{2y}\cdot 2 \\  & =8{x}^{3}y-2{z}^{4}{e}^{2y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{f}_{y}(x,y,z)=8{x}^{3}y-2{z}^{4}{e}^{2y}.
$$

Question 20
?

Find fy(x,y,z) for f(x,y,z)=4x3y2−e2yz4.

a
8x3y+4z3e2y
b
8x2y2+2z4ey
c
8x3y−2z4e2y
d
12x2y−z4ey
e
12x2y2−2z4e2y
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We differentiate the given function with respect to y, treating all other variables as constants.

First, we use the sum and constant multiple rules: fy(x,y,z)=∂∂y(4x3y2−e2yz4)=∂∂y(4x3y2)−∂∂y(e2yz4)=4x3⋅∂∂y(y2)−z4⋅∂∂y(e2y)

Then, we use the chain rule:
4x3⋅∂∂y(y2)−z4⋅∂∂y(e2y)=4x3⋅2y−z4⋅e2y⋅∂∂y(2y)=4x3⋅2y−z4⋅e2y⋅2=8x3y−2z4e2y

Therefore, fy(x,y,z)=8x3y−2z4e2y.
